intro: Health services managers run budgets, staff and operations in a complex, regulated setting. The closest of the 25 careers below are Compensation and Benefits Managers and Human Resources Managers, both at an 84% skill match; HR managers earn a BLS May 2025 median of $149,280, or 21% more than the $123,860 health managers earn.
why_it_works: Managing a hospital unit or clinic means balancing patient needs, staffing, rules and money every day. O*NET rates complex problem solving, judgment, time management and social perceptiveness at 4 out of 5 for this job. HR, finance and training management use the same leadership skills. Almost all matches need no new degree. The gaps are operational: monitoring systems and managing money.
tips: Financial Managers earn $166,570, which is 34% more, if you already own a budget.
Training and Development Managers earn $133,000, or 7% more, and suit managers who coach staff.
Get formal budget responsibility now; managing financial resources is a common gap.

faq.q: What jobs can former health services managers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Compensation and Benefits Managers (84%), Human Resources Managers (84%) and Administrative Services Managers (82%), based on O*NET 31.0. Administrative Services Managers earn $114,130, which is 8% less than the $123,860 health services median.

faq.q: Which careers for health services managers pay more?
faq.a: 13 of the 25 matches pay more. Chief Executives earn $213,990 (73% more), Computer and Information Systems Managers $175,140 (41% more) and Marketing Managers $166,790 (35% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Executive roles usually need a graduate degree.

faq.q: Do health services managers need another degree?
faq.a: Rarely. 24 of the 25 matches need no more education than health services managers already have, including all of the top 10. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 76% of workers in the closest match, so your management record in health care is what employers will weigh most.

faq.q: What skills should health services managers build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operation and control, managing financial resources, operations monitoring and troubleshooting. Time management already rates 4 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so the gap is running systems and money rather than leading people.
